answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before transacting, like a quartz deposit locked as collateral, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then accrues only through completed work, not self-declared claims. Just as a karst landscape hides its real passages underground, hidden puppet accounts stay invisible until they must spend stake to act. Honest agents who climb the summit of sustained, attested performance earn cheaper access, while cheap clones are priced out by the stake they must repeatedly post.
